title: Patch: a living arena: every tile answers a tap, and each playmat hides things in its corners to find, escalate and, rarely, surprise you
thread: **Issue #3348 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #3348: Patch: a living arena: every tile answers a tap, and each playmat hides things in its corners to find, escalate and, rarely, surprise you Opened by @jgoetzmann. ## What it does Part of #3330. The owner asked for the arena to be more interactive: "if you're clicking on the tiles, you should feel it there". Hearthstone's boards set the bar here. Each one's corners hold cosmetic clickables with their own animation and sound. Repeated clicks escalate (5 to 7 clicks for a rainbow from a waterfall), some boards hide click sequences, some outcomes are rare and random (a golden vegetable at about 1 in 1,000), and each player's board is their own. ### Today - **The mat.** Tapping empty mat (`SandSurface.tsx`, `isEmptySurfaceTarget`) leaves a mark by mat family (`TAP_FAMILY`) with a sound (`TAP_SFX`: tapWood, tapFelt, tapStone, tapNeon, tapParchment, tapAstral, sand), tuned by `SAND_FEEL`. Huge Units crack the sand or leave a crater (`slamSand`). - **Tiles.** A tile that is a legal target is a button, and swallows the tap. A tile that is not shows no feedback of its own. - **Haptics** never fire on taps or drags. - **The ten playmats** (`table-*`: tavern, wood, felt, neon-grid, marble, chessboard, desert-sand, obsidian-slab, ancient-map, astral) and ten backdrops (`field-*`, `Backdrop.tsx`) are static apart from their particles. ### What it should be 1. **Every tile answers.** Tapping or clicking any tile (`zone---`), on either side: - presses it in with a ripple in the mat's material, with that material's sound; - on a phone, adds a short haptic. A legal tile answers more strongly, and lifts to meet a dragged card (#3347). An occupied tile ripples around its card. Hovering a tile on desktop lights its edge. None of this changes what a tap does: a legal tile still plays, and an illegal one still does nothing in the game. 2. **Corners to find.** Each of the ten playmats gets two or more corner props of its own, drawn in the mat's look. Examples: a candle and a mug on the tavern; a chess knight and a clock on the chessboard; a compass and a sea serpent on the ancient map; a comet and a satellite on the astral mat; a cactus and a sand-buried skull on the desert sand. Each prop: - animates and sounds when tapped; - **escalates** with repeated taps (`CORNER_ESCALATE_TAPS`, proposed 5 to 7, to a bigger payoff: the candle flares, the knight leaps, the serpent surfaces); - has a **rare outcome** at `CORNER_RARE_CHANCE` (proposed 1 in 1,000), drawn from the client's own random source and never the game's RNG. A few mats hide a **sequence**: tap the props in the right order for a special moment. 3. **Yours alone.** Corner play is local to the player's screen, never sent to the opponent, never in the log, and never pacing or blocking the game. The opponent's half shows their own mat (R1834004), with its props still, and only yours answer you. During the animation queue's drain, props still answer, quietly. 4. **Mobile.** Corner props sit outside the lanes and the hand. Each tap target is at least `--hit-min` (R2122000), and on a phone the props fold to one per corner where room is short. The one-screen rule holds (e2e `46`, `47`). 5. **Settings.** Reduced motion keeps the sounds and shows still changes. The haptics follow the Vibration switch, and fx intensity off quiets the props to a sound. ## Acceptance - Tests: - each tile answers a tap with its material's ripple and sound; - a legal tile still fires its action; - an illegal one fires nothing in the game. - Each playmat has its props. Escalation fires at the threshold, the rare outcome at its chance (a seeded client-random test), and a hidden sequence where a mat has one. - No corner interaction reaches the net layer or the log (a test on `net.ts` and the replay). - A component spec captures each mat's corners and an escalated and a rare outcome, at desktop size and at 390x844. e2e `46` and `47` pass. - Every number is a named constant. `src/motion.test.ts` holds the new times (its `KEEP` list where they are the table's own). - The web tests, `typecheck` and `eslint` pass, and the pull request carries a `## Player note`. ## Plan _Written by `claude-2` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42341467451)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ # Plan: #3348 a living arena ## Goal Every tile (`zone---`, either side) answers a press with a press-in, a ripple in its mat's material, that material's sound and, on touch, a short haptic. A legal tile answers harder, and an occupied one ripples around its card. Hovering a tile on desktop lights its edge. Taps keep their meaning. Each of the ten playmats gets two corner props that animate, sound, escalate after 5–7 repeated taps and roll a rare outcome at 1 in 1,000. Four mats hide a tap sequence. Corner play is local to the viewer: it is never sent, never logged and never blocks the game. Nothing may cover a tile. The sidebar offsets are tuned against the component spec. - **Test churn.** Tests counting buttons on a rendered `Board` may shift by two. Fix the counts; don't hide the props. - **Purity of the game.** Props and tiles use only the cosmetic mat ids (public, R1834004). Props do not touch `onAction` or the engine, and take no `view` field. - **Audio budget.** Using only `RAPID_SFX` ids keeps prop sounds out of the game's voice cap. - **Lint scans.** The new sheet is a board sheet. The palette, spacing, surfaces and motion tests fail on a raw colour, px length, radius, shadow, z-index or unlisted time. The shadows used are rings, like `.zone[data-selected]`. - **Hotseat.** `arena/` must not read `view`. ## Open questions - **Phone portrait.** Reserving room for props there would shrink cards by roughly 15 px. This plan never does that, so on a 390x844 board props show only where measured room exists. A person should decide whether that is acceptable. - **Prop sounds.** Reusing the seven field-tap recipes (with variant and pitch) was chosen over new bespoke recipes, which would need about 20 more Web Audio recipes and test tables. - **Difficulty.** The rule does not make this harder: it is web-only, with no engine, AI, migration or crate change, and about 26 files. ````
